Title: Logistics Analyst- Border Operations
Location: Centro de San Pedro Garza García, Nuevo León, Mexico
Description: The Role The Logistics Analyst – Border Operations is responsible for supporting the execution of logistics strategies that optimize transportation performance across the United States and Mexico border network. This role focuses on transportation analytics, carrier performance management, cross-border logistics coordination, and continuous improvement initiatives that enhance service levels while reducing operational costs. The Logistics Analyst partners closely with transportation providers, customs brokers, regional operations teams, supply chain partners, and internal stakeholders across the U.S. and Mexico to ensure the efficient movement of raw materials, components, and finished goods. This position plays a critical role in maintaining operational excellence, supporting regulatory compliance, and driving sustainable logistics performance throughout Clarios’ cross-border supply chain. What You’ll Do (Impact Areas) Transportation Analytics & Performance Management Analyze transportation data, freight performance, carrier trends, and operational metrics across Over-the-Road (OTR), Intermodal (IMDL), and Rail transportation modes. Monitor logistics performance and identify opportunities to improve service levels, reduce costs, and optimize transportation networks. Develop and maintain KPIs, dashboards, and performance reports that support operational and strategic decision-making. Evaluate carrier performance, freight spend, transit times, and transportation reliability. Cross-Border Logistics Operations Support the efficient movement of freight between Mexico and the United States. Monitor shipments in transit and proactively address transportation disruptions. Ensure logistics activities align with operational requirements, customer expectations, and supply chain objectives. Support daily coordination with trucking companies, warehousing providers, customs brokers, and logistics partners. Carrier & Supplier Management Monitor transportation providers’ performance against service, cost, and operational requirements. Support carrier selection processes, shipment bids, and mini-RFQs. Analyze current and future transportation lanes to optimize carrier utilization and secure competitive rates. Assist in evaluating and selecting transportation providers and third-party logistics partners. Supply Chain Optimization & Continuous Improvement Analyze transportation and logistics data to identify inefficiencies, trends, and improvement opportunities. Lead or support initiatives focused on reducing transportation costs, improving delivery performance, and optimizing lead times. Participate in cross-functional projects aimed at improving supply chain visibility, responsiveness, and operational effectiveness. Contribute to the continuous enhancement of logistics processes and transportation strategies. Compliance & Operational Governance Ensure transportation activities comply with international trade regulations, customs requirements, and company policies. Support the drafting, implementation, and maintenance of standard operating procedures (SOPs). Monitor adherence to U.S. and Mexico transportation regulations and cross-border logistics requirements. Maintain accurate transportation data and documentation to support operational compliance. Stakeholder Collaboration Collaborate with regional logistics, transportation, and supply chain teams to ensure alignment and execution of logistics initiatives. Communicate logistics performance, risks, opportunities, and recommendations to stakeholders. Support decision-making by providing actionable analytics and operational insights. Build productive relationships with internal customers and external logistics partners. What Success Looks Like Transportation networks operate efficiently across the U.S.-Mexico border with minimal disruptions. Carrier performance meets or exceeds service, cost, and reliability expectations. Logistics KPIs provide visibility and actionable insights for continuous improvement. Transportation costs are optimized through data-driven decision-making and effective carrier management. Cross-border shipments comply with regulatory and customs requirements. Operational issues are proactively identified and resolved before impacting service. Continuous improvement initiatives generate measurable cost savings and service enhancements. Strong collaboration exists between logistics partners, carriers, and internal stakeholders. Core Competencies Transportation Analytics and Logistics Performance Management. Cross-Border Supply Chain Operations. Data Analysis and Business Insight Generation. Problem Solving and Critical Thinking. Communication and Stakeholder Management. Carrier and Supplier Relationship Management. Project Management and Execution. Continuous Improvement Mindset. Planning and Organizational Skills. Decision Making Under Pressure. Change Management and Adaptability. Attention to Detail and Data Accuracy. Customer Service Orientation. Collaboration and Teamwork. Required What You Bring (Qualifications) Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business, Industrial Engineering, or a related field. 2–5 years of experience in logistics, transportation, supply chain analytics, or related functions. Experience within manufacturing, distribution, or transportation environments. Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret large datasets and develop actionable recommendations. Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and experience with logistics or supply chain management systems. Understanding of transportation planning, inventory management, distribution, and supply chain operations. Strong organizational, prioritization, and time management skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Strong problem-solving capabilities and continuous improvement mindset. Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, cross-functional, and international environment. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and Microsoft Teams. Preferred Experience with SAP, Oracle, Transportation Management Systems (TMS), or similar logistics platforms. Experience with Power BI or other data visualization and reporting tools. Knowledge of international transportation, customs requirements, and trade compliance. Experience supporting U.S.-Mexico cross-border logistics operations. Knowledge of transportation regulations in both Mexico and the United States. Experience with OTR, Intermodal, and Rail transportation networks. Supply Chain, Logistics, or Transportation-related professional certifications. Work Model & Travel Work Model: Hybrid. Travel: Approximately 20% travel to support logistics operations, distribution centers, warehouses, carrier partners, and strategic projects. Coverage: United States and Mexico transportation network. Key Stakeholders: Transportation providers, customs brokers, warehousing partners, Supply Chain, Procurement, Operations, and regional logistics teams. Our Commitment to You Opportunity to play a key role in a complex and strategic U.S.-Mexico supply chain network. Exposure to cross-border logistics, transportation strategy, and global supply chain operations. Professional development opportunities in transportation analytics, logistics optimization, and supply chain management. A collaborative and inclusive environment focused on operational excellence and continuous improvement. The chance to contribute directly to cost optimization, service improvements, and sustainable logistics practices. Career growth opportunities within a global organization committed to innovation, performance, and customer success. Our batteries and smart solutions power nearly every type of vehicle and are found in 1 of 3 cars on the road today. Title: Business Analyst
Description: At Gratia, we believe potential is globally distributed, but opportunity is not. We bridge the gap between ambitious companies and hands-on analysts who deliver real results through a tech-enabled, apprenticeship-based platform. We focus on rigorous execution, maintaining an 88.2 NPS by supporting global partners like USA Today Co. and New York Life with precise, actionable insights. We are a remote-first community designed for professionals who value both excellence and autonomy. Why join Gratia? Flexibility and autonomy: Work with top-tier clients globally while designing a professional rhythm that suits your life. Fair global compensation meets real flexibility. Apprenticeship and growth: A curated pathway combining high-value projects with mentorship. Move from Associate Business Analyst to Lead through real work, not just theory. Community of top talent: Join a supportive network where you can share knowledge, access opportunities, and develop deep expertise to earn specialist designations in high-demand domains. The Business analyst track We are looking for specialists who are eager to solve problems alongside our project teams. This is a tiered role; your specific level will be determined during our conversations based on your technical skills, professional journey, and your readiness to manage client relationships. Associate (A2): Deliver reliable quality on standard projects, communicate directly with senior members, and navigate complex situations with curiosity. Analyst (A3): Design innovative approaches for complex challenges, exercise sound business judgment, build relationships with clients, and support the growth of junior analysts. Senior (A4): Serve as a recognized SME. You handle the most intricate challenges, set quality standards, and maintain board-level relationships. What you’ll be doing We look for individuals with transferable skills or direct experience in at least two of the following areas. Our projects are dynamic, and we encourage you to expand your toolkit as you grow with us: Financial Modeling & Analytics: From building 3-Statement models and DCF valuations to scenario-based forecasting, M&A analysis, and Monte Carlo simulations. Go-to-Market & RevOps: Optimizing sales processes, CRM configurations, and growth planning to drive revenue. Process Design & Automation: Mapping workflows and implementing tools like Zapier/Make to build high-efficiency systems. Data Analytics & Visualizations: Transforming complex datasets into Tableau/Power BI visualizations and ML-powered insights. Market Intelligence: Conducting TAM/SAM/SOM analysis, competitive research, and crafting industry-specific narratives. Narrative & Design: Developing investor-ready decks, executive presentations, and high-stakes visual communication. Business Planning & Growth: Developing corporate roadmaps, conducting SWOT analyses, and building growth frameworks or risk assessments. Project Management & Delivery: Planning and executing complex initiatives, managing everything from risk registers and resource allocation to stakeholder alignment. What we’re looking for Core competencies: Decision excellence: The ability to structure challenges and develop actionable solutions. Business acumen: A solid grasp of business models and how analysis connects to real-world outcomes. Execution mastery: Delivering "Reference-Quality" work that is accurate, timely, and polished. Stakeholder impact: Communicating with clarity and presence across all levels of an organization. Flexibility & agility: A steep learning curve on new tools and the ability to thrive in evolving environments. Qualifications: We value a blend of technical capability and adaptive thinking: Experience leading client conversations and providing high-level guidance. Experience from MBB (McKinsey, Bain, BCG), Big 4, or another recognized firm is a huge plus. A natural interest in data-driven storytelling and a desire to work with modern, AI-enhanced workflows. A professional tone with the ability to explain complex ideas simply. A flexible schedule that allows for a consistent daily overlap with US business hours. Why Gratia is your next step Designed for independent professionals who want the freedom of private practice with the support of a global community. We offer both part-time and full-time options. Compensation is tailored to your tier and your evolving portfolio of expertise. Elevate your profile by working directly with leaders at innovative global organizations like USA Today Co., Endeavor, and New York Life. Your growth is guided by transparent requirements—AQS, Peer Review, and Client Feedback—putting you in the driver's seat of your career.

Title: Lead Analytics Engineer, Data Governance & Platform
Description: About LawnStarter LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $150M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for all home services, operating across three brands (LawnStarter, Lawn Love, Home Gnome) on a single shared platform. About Analytics At LawnStarter We're a small, senior analytics team supporting the entire company: product, marketing, operations, and finance all run on the data we serve. The foundation is solid. A centralized Redshift data warehouse holds all source data, modeled in dbt and orchestrated by Airflow, with Segment feeding event data in. You won't be stitching scattered sources together. The platform exists, and your job is to make it trustworthy and keep it that way. We're mid-migration to Lightdash as our single BI platform, replacing Tableau and Metabase. Data governance is becoming a dedicated function here. You'll be its first dedicated owner, building it alongside the Data Director. The Role You'll own LawnStarter's data governance area and build it: the person who turns the governance agenda into working systems (monitors, checks, lineage, metric definitions, tracking standards) with your own hands. You'll grow the function together with the Data Director, at the pace demand and impact call for. If you want it and the skills are there, you could become its manager one day. "Lead" here means technical weight first. You're the reference the analysts turn to when a pipeline misbehaves, a metric definition gets contentious, or an event's data looks wrong, and the example that raises the bar for how governance work gets done. As the function grows, your leadership can widen with it. What Makes This Role Different Build, don't chase. Your job is the machinery that catches data problems before stakeholders do: automation and monitors, not manual firefighting Whole-stack surface. Source data to pipelines to dashboards and ML models. Your work touches the entire chain, not one slice of it A live migration to shape. Lightdash is landing now, and the semantic layer just shipped for our most critical metrics. You'll do the defining, mapping, and tidying work that decides whether they stay trustworthy An area to grow. Governance doesn't have a fixed shape here yet. You'll decide with the Data Director what the function takes on next and how it grows What You'll Own Quality and freshness machinery, building and scaling the automated monitoring (freshness checks, schema-change alerts, anomaly monitors) that catches upstream changes before they break anything downstream, and running incidents to resolution Semantic-layer coverage, the long tail of metrics that still needs definition and mapping, done to the one-metric-one-definition standard, plus the hygiene that keeps the layer tidy as it grows Event-catalog operations, reviewing new Segment events against our governed catalog's standards, keeping the catalog matched to what production actually sends, and investigating drift when detection flags it Lineage tooling, extending our lineage map beyond dbt (Segment events and Lightdash need stitching in) so downstream impact of a production change can be assessed before it ships Lightdash hygiene, the hands-on side of workspace health: certification, naming, permissions upkeep, and keeping self-serve content findable and trustworthy The data roadmap, increasingly, working with the Data Director to turn what product, marketing, ops, and finance need from data into priorities for the platform, and owning more of that roadmap as the function grows Scope here widens with demand and with what your work proves. As the function takes on more, more of it becomes yours to run, including helping hire the people it adds. Problems to Solve Take detection from partial to comprehensive An AI-powered Analytics Engineer agent already runs freshness monitoring, dbt job monitoring, and dbt-based lineage checks, but not yet at the scale or coverage we need. You'll extend it until "a stakeholder found the problem first" stops happening. Map the long tail of the semantic layer Our most critical metrics have one governed definition each, in code. Well over a hundred more still need defining and mapping: unglamorous, high-judgment work where every shortcut becomes someone's wrong number later. Keep the event catalog honest Segment events are implemented by many engineers across many teams, and entropy is relentless: new events drift from standards, and existing ones silently degrade when features change. The guardrails exist. You're the person who runs them and catches what they miss. Turn business needs into a data roadmap Every area of the company wants something from data, and today those asks reach the Analytics team as a stream of interruptions. With the Data Director, you'll turn them into priorities that balance stakeholder needs against platform health. The hard part: saying "not yet" to important people, with a reason they respect. What Success Looks Like (Year 1) The monitors you built catch problems before stakeholders do, pipeline and freshness incidents get found by automation, not by someone opening a stale dashboard The semantic layer's long tail is mapped, every reported metric has exactly one governed definition, and arguments about whose number is right don't happen Event reviews run on a steady cadence, new events ship compliant, drift gets investigated within days, and the catalog matches production You're the acknowledged technical reference, when something data-related looks wrong anywhere in the company, people know who to bring it to, and you usually already know Data-trust asks come to you, stakeholders bring their data-quality and governance requests to you directly, and you hold a slice of the roadmap with the Data Director Requirements Who You Are Governance is your craft, not your chore. You enjoy making data systems trustworthy and tidy. You're the person who can't leave a broken naming convention alone. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you see governance as a stepping stone to "real" analytics work AI-native. You use AI tools (Claude Code, Copilot, ChatGPT) daily to build quality checks, write automation, triage anomalies, and document as you go. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you're skeptical of AI tools or prefer to do everything manually A hands-on builder at a lead bar. You write the SQL, debug the Airflow DAG, and ship the monitor yourself, and the way you do it becomes the way the team does it. This is unlikely to be a good fit if your instinct is to spec work for someone else to execute Automation-first. Your instinct for any recurring check is to build a monitor, not a checklist. This is unlikely to be a good fit if your quality practice depends on manual review and discipline A technical reference people seek out. You explain clearly, answer patiently, and leave people smarter. Your influence comes from that, before any title does. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you need formal authority to get people to follow a standard Open to growing with the function. If the area grows into a team and leading it suits you, you're open to developing the management side to get there. If it doesn't, staying the technical lead of this area is a full, senior role here, not a consolation prize. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you'd take the role mainly for the title it might lead to This Role Is NOT A BI analyst role. You won't spend your days building dashboards for stakeholders. You build the machinery that keeps everyone else's dashboards trustworthy A title with a timeline, or a guarantee. There's no promotion date. If the role grows into managing the function, the Manager title follows the work you're already doing. If the function needs a manager before that happens, or the fit isn't there, we'd hire one, and you'd remain the technical lead of the area A hands-off role. The building is the job now, and it stays core as your scope grows. If you want to step away from the keyboard, this isn't it Tech You'll Touch Warehouse & pipelines - Redshift, dbt, Airflow Ingestion - Fivetran, plus custom Airflow pipelines Event tracking - Segment BI - Lightdash (primary), Tableau and Metabase (sunsetting) AI tooling - Claude Code, Codex, Brain (our internal AI toolkit), and any tool that makes you more effective or efficient Observability - an AI-powered Analytics Engineer agent (freshness monitoring, dbt job monitoring, dbt lineage) you'll extend, plus the quality and impact tooling you'll build around it You don't need every box checked. You need hands-on depth in the warehouse/pipeline layer and the instinct to automate what others check manually. Benefits Base salary: $75k-$100k/year (contractor arrangement, standard for our Latin America-based team; no equity) Fully remote: This work needs deep focus, building monitors, untangling pipelines, and we trust you to manage your environment. Async collaboration is the norm Flexible PTO: We focus on results. Take what you need LawnStarter provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or genetics. We comply with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment.

Title: Delivery Pod Lead, Americas
Description: About Hilbert Hilbert is a scalable, data science-first growth engine that gives B2C teams predictive clarity into user behavior, revenue drivers, and the actions that drive sustainable growth. Fully agentic by design, Hilbert shrinks months-long decision cycles to minutes. From Fortune 10 enterprises to beloved brands like FreshDirect, Blank Street, and Levain Bakery, operators run their growth on Hilbert. We're also co-building alongside leading AI companies. The Mission: Turn Signed Deals Into Working Data Foundations Hilbert has two parts: a data foundation that gives our AI agents a high-fidelity view of each business, and an agentic web app where growth teams find and act on insights. For enterprise customers, the data foundation runs either on our managed ClickHouse stack or warehouse-native inside the customer's own Databricks, Snowflake or BigQuery. The hard problem Every enterprise customer is different, but our AI must reason the same way wherever the data lives. Your team turns messy, unique customer data into a consistent data foundation and ML, fast, and you decide how each delivery gets done. We want every pod to stay lean and efficient across very different customer environments, delivering quality work at startup speed. What You'll Do Lead and grow a small team of data and ML engineers who will be delivering the data foundation. Review solution designs and proof-of-concept scopes before they reach customers, and decide what can be delivered and how. Own each delivery after signature: staff it with the right engineers, and own its plan, timeline and quality. Stay hands-on in architecture, data discovery, canonical modeling, semantic layers, ETL and ELT orchestration across customer and Hilbert environments, secure cloud integration, and reviews of feature and model work. Title: Analista Senior de Desarrollo de Negocios, Ventas
Description: Somos una empresa liderada por personas, empoderada por la tecnología, omnicanal, dedicada a ayudar a la gente a ahorrar dinero y vivir mejor. En 2009, Walmart de México y Walmart Centroamérica iniciamos una nueva etapa de crecimiento y nos convertimos en un gran equipo. A partir de 2010, somos Walmart de México y Centroamérica, una de las cadenas comerciales más importantes de la región. Nuestra estrategia omnicanal está centrada en nuestros clientes y en mejorar su experiencia de compra. Estamos presentes en 6 países: México, Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua y Costa Rica. Contamos con 4,079 tiendas en la región, de las cuales 3,154 están en México y 925 en Centroamérica. Actualmente 6 millones de clientes compran en nuestras tiendas y clubes cada día en México y Centroamérica. Continuamos ofreciendo a nuestros clientes los productos que necesitan a precios bajos, a través de nuestro portafolio con diversos formatos que tienen propuestas de valor únicas. Al mismo tiempo, aceleramos nuestra estrategia de digitalización. Todo ello, con el fin de servir mejor a todos nuestros clientes y socios en sus diferentes misiones de compra, en todos nuestros canales. Descripción del empleo En Walmart de México y Centroamérica buscamos un Analista Senior de Desarrollo de Negocios, que logre contrinuir al éxito de las campañas publicitarias de Walmart Connect mediante la planeación estratégica, seguimiento, análisis y optimización de iniciativas de Retail Media. Responsabilidades Desarrollar planes de medios alineados con los objetivos comerciales y de marketing de los anunciantes. Diseñar estrategias de Retail Media considerando formatos onsite y offsite para maximizar resultados. Analizar inventario, audiencias, formatos publicitarios y KPIs para generar recomendaciones estratégicas basadas en datos. Monitorear el desempeño de campañas activas e identificar oportunidades de optimización. Elaborar reportes ejecutivos, dashboards e insights que permitan evaluar resultados y generar recomendaciones para futuras campañas. Presentar estrategias y resultados a clientes, agencias y stakeholders internos de manera clara y efectiva. Colaborar estrechamente con los equipos de KAM, Client Success, Planning, AdOps y Performance para garantizar una correcta ejecución de las campañas. Participar en la etapa final de las campañas comunicando resultados, aprendizajes y oportunidades de mejora. Experiencia desarrollando estrategias de medios y recomendaciones para anunciantes. Experiencia en análisis de campañas y generación de reportes de desempeño. Experiencia trabajando de la mano con equipos comerciales, clientes o agencias. Capacidad para transformar datos en insights y recomendaciones accionables. Title: Forward Deployed Growth Partner, LATAM
Description: About Hilbert Hilbert is a scalable, data science-first growth engine that gives B2C teams predictive clarity into user behavior, revenue drivers, and the actions that drive sustainable growth. Fully agentic by design, Hilbert shrinks months-long decision cycles to minutes. From Fortune 10 enterprises to beloved brands like FreshDirect, Blank Street, and Levain Bakery, operators run their growth on Hilbert. We're backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). Forward Deployed Growth Engineers are a new, dedicated customer team at Hilbert, sitting in our Foundations Tribe. You'll work hand in hand with our Growth Science and Product teams, who own the product's logic, models and playbooks, and take that expertise into every customer, from the first meeting to the moment Hilbert is running their growth. What the role is This is customer success delivered with growth expertise. You'll join each of your accounts as soon as the lead comes in. You'll help shape the use cases during the sales cycle and keep owning the account through deployment and live usage. You own two commercial outcomes: proof-of-concept conversion and existing account revenue growth . We also measure time to first value, sustained product adoption and the share of routine customer needs you handle independently. Two things make this role different from most customer success jobs. First, you're forward-deployed: you'll travel with our GTM team around 50% of the time, sit in the room with our customers' leadership, and become the person they call when they want to move faster. Second, you're a growth operator, not a ticket handler: our customers buy growth, and you'll help them own their use cases in Hilbert, from paid media, CRM and retention to discounts, merchandising and demand forecasting, and read the results back with them . You are expected to develop a deep understanding of Hilbert’s capabilities, communicate clearly and effectively with customers, and proactively manage customer relationships to maximize the value delivered to every customer. You'll be part of the first cohort of this team, reporting to the Head of Forward Deployed Growth in our Foundations Tribe and working day to day with the GTM team and delivery engineering pod in your region. You'll learn our data sources, deployment methods and the problems our customers bring us alongside our Growth Science, Product and data teams, and you'll handle most routine customer needs independently. When an account needs deeper expertise, you'll bring in our subject-matter experts and turn what you learn into answers, case studies and examples the whole team reuses. What you'll do Own a portfolio of accounts end-to-end: get assigned as soon as a lead comes in, shape the use cases with GTM and sales engineering through close, and stay accountable for onboarding coordination, customer follow-ups and blocker tracking. Convert pilots into long-term partnerships: define success criteria with the customer up front, keep the proof of concept on track, and make the business case for expansion with numbers you can defend. Grow account revenue: find the next highest-impact use case inside each customer and turn it into new scope. Be the customer's trusted growth advisor: lead demos and working sessions, help customers put agreed use cases into practice, train their teams, review results, and identify what is blocking adoption. Drive real business transformation: go beyond usage and make sure the results change how the customer's business runs. Get the customer's data in: scope the data each use case needs, agree with their data team how it reaches Hilbert, and run the timeline with our data engineers until it is usable. Do it again whenever a new use case needs new data. Capture how each customer measures their business: their KPIs, definitions and business rules, set up in Hilbert so every answer matches their numbers. Manage every stakeholder: from the C-level sponsor to the marketing, growth and data teams who use Hilbert every day, and keep them aligned as the account grows. Build rapport in person: travel with our GTM team around 50% of the time, shadow and then lead customer sessions, and know the product better than anyone else in the room. Cover most customer needs yourself, and know when to escalate: you are expected to handle around 80% of customer needs independently from the very first assignment, building toward the capability to cover 95% of everything a customer brings. For everything else, engage our Growth Science, Product, and Data teams efficiently by providing clear customer context, business impact, relevant evidence, and what you have already investigated. Respect their time by minimizing unnecessary meetings and prioritizing clear, asynchronous communication. Own the follow-up, keep the customer informed, and ensure key learnings feed into the product roadmap. Expand across departments and use cases: map which other teams (paid media, CRM, merchandising, pricing, finance) can run their decisions on Hilbert, find the next highest-impact use case in each, and turn it into new scope. Embed Hilbert into activation surfaces: connect Hilbert’s outputs to the tools where the customer’s teams already act, from ad platforms and CRM/CDP to promo, merchandising and planning systems, so every insight flows straight into execution and becomes part of the daily workflow. Join GTM funnel reviews: take part in the regular funnel reviews with the GTM team, and know which leads are coming to you next. Grow the shared library: add answers, case studies and customer examples, so expert guidance becomes something the whole team reuses. What you bring Around 5 to 8 years of experience: an engineering or natural sciences background, followed by an analytical role in management consulting or a similar setting; pure customer success leaders with a strong analytical edge are also welcome. Strongly analytical: you write SQL and understand customer data sources, key business definitions, data coverage and freshness, and the meaning and limitations of model outputs well enough to explain them and investigate routine questions. You can build a business case and present it to a CFO or CMO. Driven by real business transformation: insight isn't enough until it changes how the customer's business runs. Continuous learning: you don't know insurance or grocery yet, and you'll figure it out fast. You're a problem solver who hacks most of the job yourself and knows exactly who to bring in for the rest. Excellent with customers: polished and high-energy, at ease in every customer conversation from small talk to the boardroom, credible with senior stakeholders, and able to build relationships that outlast a single project. Strong stakeholder management is a must: you navigate complex organizations and keep senior and day-to-day stakeholders aligned. Happy to travel often across your region, around 50% of the time and sometimes to a different customer city every week, and to work with an owner's mindset in a fast-moving startup. Fluent in English and Spanish. Nice to have: deep vertical expertise in retail, grocery, or financial services, or existing relationships with enterprise B2C companies. Portuguese is a plus. Reporting and location You report to the Head of Forward Deployed Growth and work closely with our GTM leadership in Latin America, as the growth counterpart to the region’s GTM team. You’re on the move with GTM, joining new leads and customer meetings from the first conversation. Our Growth Science and Product teams own the product’s logic, models and playbooks, train you on them and support you on the deepest problems, and our delivery engineering team builds and runs each deployment with you. You are based in Latin America, ideally Mexico City or Lima. The role may start remotely while we build Hilbert’s regional presence, with travel to customers across the region of around 50 percent, and relocation within Latin America may be needed as our hub takes shape. Compensation Base salary, plus variable pay tied to performance and the revenue you help drive (proof-of-concept conversion, renewals and expansion), plus equity. Details are shared in next steps. Interview process Recruiter screen, 30 minutes. GTM interview with the GTM leadership in Latin America, 30 minutes: a customer relationship you owned, from first meeting to live usage or expansion, and how you managed the stakeholders along the way. Hiring manager interview, 30 minutes: how you work with customers and with our Growth, Product and GTM teams. Growth case with our Growth team, 60 minutes: a real customer case, from the business problem and the data it needs to the use case, the success criteria and the business case for expansion. Team and final interviews: meet the people you’ll work with day to day, and our leadership. References: two from clients, one from a colleague you worked with on customer accounts. Why join us At Hilbert, we move fast, work collaboratively, and give people real ownership over their impact. As a fast-growing company, there's no shortage of room to grow — you'll take on new challenges quickly and shape the path as you go. On top of that, here’s how we take care of our team: Work from anywhere. Two weeks a year to take your laptop somewhere new, whether that’s a beach in Mallorca or your family’s kitchen table. Sharpen your English. Business English classes, for when the boardroom pitch needs to land perfectly. And many more. We’re always cooking up new ways to support our team. Come build the future with us, and grow alongside a company that’s investing in yours. Hilbert is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to building a diverse team and an inclusive culture, and we welcome applicants of all backgrounds. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law.
